reason: The three frozen memories were called development-score-equivalent because their ordered family-level outcome triples were all zero, but the historical development rows were collected on different task identities. They therefore were not evaluated on one common current probe panel. Different-task equal scores cannot identify evaluation-state equivalence.
additional_quality_issue: The historical family-level signature was a complete floor: every retrieved, placebo, and no-memory development score was zero. Even with common task identities, a complete floor would be a weak paper-level state-equivalence witness because the current evaluation carries little discriminatory information.
replacement_protocol_requirements: Every compared memory must be evaluated on exactly the same current probe task IDs.
The current evaluation signature must be exactly equal across memories.
The common current panel must be non-degenerate; complete all-zero or complete all-one signatures are not accepted as paper-level qualification.
The future panel must be sealed before current-panel outcomes are observed.
Future divergence must be measured against a token-matched placebo and reproducible no-memory control.
Failure to qualify current equivalence is a substrate stop and does not falsify the broader evaluation-aliasing hypothesis.
